chunks.text: 58-year-old male, Production Craftsman or Related Worker, resident of Pasir Ris, Singapore.
History of pneumonia resolved 5 years ago
Remote history of left femoral fracture (age 25), fully healed
Previous use of Omeprazole for GERD, discontinued 2 years ago

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your surgery tomorrow. I'd like to go through some questions to make sure we're all set for your laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anesthesia. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I'm ready. I want to make sure everything goes smoothly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. You've been diagnosed with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. Are you currently managing these conditions with your medications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I take my medications regularly. I'm on Atorvastatin 20mg once daily for cholesterol, Metformin 500mg twice daily for diabetes, and Lisinopril 10mg once daily for blood pressure.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. I also see that you were on Aspirin 75mg once daily, but the records mention it's still active. Can you confirm the current antiplatelet medication and the reason for any changes from Aspirin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, right. I actually stopped taking Aspirin about six months ago because it was giving me stomach discomfort. My cardiologist then put me on Clopidogrel 75mg once daily instead for secondary prevention of heart issues.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. That's important to know. Thank you for clarifying. Now, regarding allergies, you mentioned a rash with Penicillin. Any other allergies we should be aware of?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just Penicillin. That's the only one.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, were there any complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had a hernia repair about 10 years ago. The anesthesia was fine then, no problems at all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Now, about your current condition—how has the gallbladder issue been affecting you? Any episodes of pain, especially after eating?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I get this sharp pain on the right side, especially after fatty meals. It's been happening more often, so the doctor said it's best to remove it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. And finally, have you fasted as instructed? Nothing by mouth after midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had dinner early last night and only sipped water this morning. Nothing else since then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Just one more thing—do you have any concerns or questions about the anesthesia or the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I think you've covered everything. I'm just ready to get this done and feel better.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great, Mr. Tan. We'll take good care of you. I'll see you in the holding area before the surgery. Any issues, just give us a call.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thank you, doctor. I appreciate it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] iv access established, two large bore peripheral lines

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] fluid bolus one thousand milliliters normal saline

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] hypotension noted, mean arterial pressure forty five, atenolol infusion started

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:35] maintenance infusion of remifentanil zero point two micrograms per kilogram per minute initiated

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:50] intraoperative peak airway pressure twenty eight cm h2o, checked tube position, no change

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm a bit tired, but okay. My tummy is sore, and I feel a little nauseous.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I understand. On a scale from 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4 or 5. It's manageable, but I can feel it.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for letting me know. Have you felt any sickness or vomited at all since coming out of anesthesia?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, not yet. Just a bit of a queasy feeling, but I haven't thrown up.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. How about your breathing? Any shortness of breath or discomfort in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I'm breathing fine. Just a bit of a sore throat from the tube, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's common after intubation. Do you remember anything from the surgery itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember anything. I was out completely.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected. Since you have hypertension and diabetes, we'll keep a close eye on your vitals and blood sugar levels. Any other concerns for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all for now. Thank you, doctor.

58-year-old male, ASA-PS II, undergoing elective Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy under General Anesthesia with endotracheal intubation for gallbladder issue presenting with sharp pain on the right side, especially after fatty meals.

Patient has a history of Hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, and Hyperlipidemia. Current medications include Atorvastatin, Metformin, Lisinopril, and Clopidogrel. No known drug allergies except for Penicillin (rash).

Intraoperative complications included hypotension (MAP 45 mmHg) and elevated peak airway pressure (28 cm H2O). Patient received Propofol, Remifentanil, and a fluid bolus. Endotracheal tube placed with grade one view.

Monitor for PONV due to history of GERD and opioid use; watch airway for potential obstruction due to elevated intraoperative peak airway pressure; manage blood glucose levels due to Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus; carefully manage blood pressure due to history of hypertension and intraoperative hypotension; consider increased bleeding risk due to Clopidogrel use.
Patient reports being a bit tired but okay, with sore abdomen and mild nausea.
Patient rates current pain as 4 or 5 on a scale of 0 to 10, describing it as manageable.
Patient experiences a queasy feeling but has not vomited since emerging from anesthesia.
Patient reports no shortness of breath or chest discomfort, only a sore throat attributed to intubation.
Patient recalls nothing from the surgery, consistent with effective general anesthesia.
Provider notes the need for close monitoring of vitals and blood sugar levels due to patient's hypertension and diabetes.
Intraoperative hypotension was managed with atenolol infusion.
Patient was induced with propofol 120mg and had a grade 1 view upon intubation.
